questions.passage: Then the voice on the other end usually said, “Could you tell him so-and-so called?” Since I was still learning English, I was never able to make out who this was, so I needed to ask, “Could you please spell it out?” so I could write it down.
questions.prompt: What is the caller usually asking the narrator to do?
questions.promptZh: 来电者通常请求作者做什么？
options: Tell Mike that a particular person has called.
Tell the caller that Mike has changed his name.
Ask Mike to spell the narrator's name.
Keep the call secret from Mike.
optionsZh: 告诉 Mike 某某打过电话。
告诉来电者 Mike 改名了。
让 Mike 拼出作者姓名。
向 Mike 隐瞒这通电话。
analyses: A tell him...called 是请代传来电信息，so-and-so 代指某个来电人。
B 没有改名。
C 后文拼写请求由作者提出，不能移给 Mike。
D tell 与隐瞒相反；usually 保留习惯性而非每通电话必然如此。

vocabulary.context: 代指来电者的姓名，是泛指表达，不是这位来电者真的叫 So-and-so。
vocabulary.example: She said that so-and-so had left a message.

questions.translation: 电话另一头通常接着说：“能告诉他某某来过电话吗？”由于我还在学英语，总听不清对方是谁，就需要问：“能请你拼出来吗？”这样才能记下。

evidence.quote: Then the voice on the other end usually said, “Could you tell him so-and-so called?”

questions.prompt: Why does the narrator ask the caller to spell the name?
questions.promptZh: 作者为什么请来电者拼写姓名？
options: To test how well the caller knows Mike.
To obtain a written record of a name he cannot make out by ear.
To avoid giving Mike any message.
To correct the caller's English pronunciation.
optionsZh: 测试来电者是否熟悉 Mike。
把听不清的姓名记录下来。
避免给 Mike 传递任何信息。
纠正来电者英语发音。
analyses: A 没有测试关系的动机。
B since...still learning English 与 so I could write it down 构成原因和目的链。
C 正是为了能记录，不是拒绝传话。
D 请拼写不等于纠正对方发音；保留作者自己的听力困难。

vocabulary.context: it 承接需要辨认和拼写的来电者姓名，不是整段通话逐字记录。
vocabulary.example: Please write it down before you forget the address.
collocations: so I could write it down

questions.passage: One day, I got a call and followed the same routine. When I asked the speaker’s name, he spelled out, “H-I-S-F-A-T-H-E-R.”
questions.prompt: What is meant by 'followed the same routine' here?
questions.promptZh: 这里 followed the same routine 是什么意思？
options: He repeated his journey from Tokyo to Maine.
He began a completely new method of answering calls.
He used his familiar procedure for dealing with a caller's identity.
He followed Mike to a college class.
optionsZh: 他重复东京到缅因的旅程。
他开始用全新方法接电话。
他沿用询问来电者身份的惯常程序。
他跟着 Mike 去上课。
analyses: A routine 是接电话的处理方式，不是旅行路线。
B same 与全新相反。
C 下一句 When I asked the speaker's name 与前面的惯常询问相接。
D follow 在此不是跟随某人走路。

vocabulary.context: 指已叙述的电话应对流程，不是体育训练或交通路线。
vocabulary.example: The assistant followed the usual routine when taking a message.

questions.translation: 有一天，我接到电话，照同样的程序应对。询问来电者姓名时，他拼出：“H-I-S-F-A-T-H-E-R。”

evidence.quote: One day, I got a call and followed the same routine. When I asked the speaker’s name, he spelled out, “H-I-S-F-A-T-H-E-R.”

questions.passage: I repeated, “H-I-S-F-A-T-H-E-R?” “Yes.” “Great, thanks.” I hung up.
questions.prompt: What does the caller's 'Yes' confirm in this exchange?
questions.promptZh: 这段对话里，来电者的 Yes 确认了什么？
options: That Mike has answered the telephone.
That the narrator has already understood the family relationship.
That the narrator has repeated the spelled sequence correctly.
That Reese wants the narrator to leave the car.
optionsZh: Mike 已经接听电话。
作者已经理解亲属关系。
作者重复的拼写序列无误。
Reese 要作者下车。
analyses: A 接电话的是作者。
B 确认字母不等于确认理解，后文才意识到是 Mike 父亲。
C Yes 紧接 H-I-S-F-A-T-H-E-R 的复述，确认所说序列。
D 把另一段汽车谈话误移到电话场景。

vocabulary.context: 这里确认复述的拼写；其含义应由紧邻前文确定。

questions.translation: 我重复：“H-I-S-F-A-T-H-E-R？”“对。”“好的，谢谢。”我挂断了电话。

evidence.quote: I repeated, “H-I-S-F-A-T-H-E-R?” “Yes.” “Great, thanks.” I hung up.

questions.passage: It was humiliating. Indeed, I had never been more humiliated. But this incident made me realize that many immigrants in the U.S. experience similar humiliation, as do many less fortunate people in Japan.
questions.prompt: What does 'humiliating' describe in the narrator's reflection?
questions.promptZh: 作者反思中 humiliating 描述什么？
options: The caller deliberately insults Mike.
The incident leaves the narrator feeling deeply embarrassed.
Reese is ashamed of his choice of music.
Every immigrant reports exactly the same event.
optionsZh: 来电者故意侮辱 Mike。
这件事让作者深感难堪。
Reese 为自己的音乐喜好羞愧。
每位移民报告完全相同的事件。
analyses: A 没有证据证明来电者有故意羞辱的动机。
B humiliating 描述作者自己的强烈难堪体验。
C 不属于音乐对话中 Reese 的情绪。
D similar 不等于事件完全一样，many 也不是 every。

vocabulary.meaning: 令人难堪的；使人感到受辱的
vocabulary.context: 指作者体验，不自动证明对方有恶意。
vocabulary.example: Forgetting a simple word in public felt humiliating to him.

questions.translation: 这太让我难堪了。事实上，我从未如此难堪。但这件事让我意识到，美国许多移民也有类似的屈辱感，日本许多处境较不利的人也是如此。

evidence.quote: It was humiliating. Indeed, I had never been more humiliated. But this incident made me realize that many immigrants in the U.S. experience similar humiliation, as do many less fortunate people in Japan.

questions.passage: Until my “his father” incident, I hadn’t thought about how my experience as an exchange student would be similar to immigrants’ experiences in the U.S. Until then, I hadn’t identified myself with other immigrants at all. Of course, I also had a lot of awesome experiences while studying abroad, like going to Acadia National Park and Martha’s Vineyard, where I saw rocky beaches and lighthouses for the first time. This wide range of unexpected experiences and unusual emotions makes studying abroad extremely psychologically rich and rewarding in the long run.
questions.prompt: What new sights does the narrator associate with the two trips?
questions.promptZh: 作者把哪两种首次见到的景象与这两次游览联系起来？
options: Desert dunes and ancient temples.
Tea fields and mountain orchards.
Skyscrapers and underground stations.
Rocky beaches and lighthouses.
optionsZh: 沙丘与古庙。
茶田与山地果园。
摩天楼与地铁站。
岩石海岸与灯塔。
analyses: A 本句未提沙漠寺庙。
B 属于其他场景的联想，非这两地描述。
C 不是作者所列初见景物。
D where I saw rocky beaches and lighthouses for the first time 明示两项；Of course, also 补入积极体验，不否认先前难堪。

vocabulary.context: 与 rocky beaches 一起构成作者当时新见的海岸景象。
vocabulary.example: The boat passed several lighthouses along the coast.

questions.translation: “his father”事件之前，我没想过交换生经历会与美国移民相似，也完全没把自己与其他移民联系起来。当然，留学时也有很多精彩体验，如去 Acadia 国家公园和 Martha’s Vineyard，第一次看到岩石海岸与灯塔。这样广泛的意外经历与不同寻常的情绪，让留学心理上极其丰富，并在长远中带来回报。

evidence.quote: Of course, I also had a lot of awesome experiences while studying abroad, like going to Acadia National Park and Martha’s Vineyard, where I saw rocky beaches and lighthouses for the first time.

questions.passage: Traveling abroad as a tourist is also novel and interesting, but as a tourist you rarely have authentic interactions with locals. Living abroad is much more challenging and evokes a wider range of emotions. In short, psychological richness requires a lot of ingredients, not just novelty but also challenges and perspective change.
questions.prompt: Which limitation does the author attach to being a tourist abroad?
questions.promptZh: 作者对以游客身份出国指出了什么局限？
options: Tourists rarely have authentic interactions with local people.
Tourists can never find anything novel.
Tourists always experience a wider emotional range than residents.
Tourists are unable to enter museums or concerts.
optionsZh: 游客很少与本地人有真实深入的互动。
游客绝不可能遇到新奇事物。
游客总比居住者体验更多情绪。
游客不能进入博物馆或音乐会。
analyses: A rarely have authentic interactions with locals 是限定性概括。
B 前半句承认 also novel and interesting。
C 下一句反而强调生活海外更具挑战、情绪更多。
D 未说游客进不了文化场所；rarely 不能改成从不可能。

vocabulary.context: 修饰与本地人的互动质量，不是商品真伪或护照合法性。
vocabulary.example: Sharing a meal gave them an authentic conversation with local residents.

questions.translation: 以游客身份出国也新奇有趣，但游客很少与本地人有真实深入的互动。在国外生活更具挑战，也唤起更广泛的情绪。总之，心理丰富需要多种成分，不仅新奇，也有挑战和视角变化。

evidence.quote: Traveling abroad as a tourist is also novel and interesting, but as a tourist you rarely have authentic interactions with locals.
